key_insight: OmniRobotHome demonstrates that a synchronized multi-camera platform plus an occlusion-aware, low-latency 3D tracking pipeline can enable reliable real-time multiadic human–robot interaction in cluttered home environments where persistent occlusion and rapid state changes previously blocked progress.
problem_solved: Addresses the central bottleneck for multiadic home HRI: achieving robust, real-time 3D tracking of multiple humans, robots, and objects under close-proximity interaction with heavy occlusion and fast state changes.
method: Synchronized multi-camera rig providing dense multi-view RGB/depth coverage to reduce blind spots and persistent occlusions.
Occlusion-aware multi-agent state estimation that fuses per-view detections into consistent 3D poses (humans, robots, objects) and maintains identity through rapid interactions.
Low-latency end-to-end software pipeline optimized for concurrent tracking and streaming to support real-time control and interaction.
impact: Enables researchers and practitioners to develop, test, and benchmark real-time multi-agent perception and control for realistic home scenarios, unlocking safer and more coordinated multi-human multi-robot behavior in real-world deployments.
visual_elements: System diagram: multi-camera layout around a home scene with arrows showing synchronized capture and fusion into a single 3D workspace.
Before/after sequence: single-view occluded tracking failure vs. multi-view recovered 3D poses overlayed on the scene.
Latency & accuracy chart: real-time pipeline throughput and tracking accuracy under increasing occlusion density.
Illustration of multiadic interaction: multiple humans and robots collaboratively manipulating objects with 3D skeletons and object bounding volumes.
paper_title: OmniRobotHome: A Multi-Camera Platform for Real-Time Multiadic Human-Robot Interaction
paper_authors: Junyoung Lee, Sookwan Han, Jeonghwan Kim, Inhee Lee, Mingi Choi
